title: Linear feature identifiability and Gaussian MAP tests

items.title: Exact linear feature estimability through the adjoint range
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a real Hilbert space and let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space. Let $K:X\to H$ be bounded and linear, let $\epsilon>0$, and let $Z$ be a jointly Gaussian centered family indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$. For each $x\in X$ define $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$. A continuous linear feature is a map $\phi\in X^*$, where $X^*$ is the continuous dual of $X$. By the Riesz representation theorem there is a unique $h_\phi\in X$ with $\phi(x)=\langle x,h_\phi\rangle_X$ for every $x\in X$. The feature is **exactly linearly estimable by one probe** if some $\Phi\in H$ makes the statistic $Y_x(\Phi)$ unbiased for $\phi(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Writing $R(K^*)=\{K^*\Phi:\Phi\in H\}$ for the adjoint range, this holds exactly when $h_\phi\in R(K^*)$. Every such probe has variance $\epsilon^2\|\Phi\|_H^2$. This definition concerns one-probe unbiased linear estimators; it does not identify membership in $\overline{R(K^*)}$ with exact estimability.
items.strategy: Characterize unbiasedness by matching the adjoint mean to the Riesz feature vector and compute the probe variance.

references.title: Remo Kretschmann and Frank Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, §1.1 and §1.2
Remo Kretschmann, Tanja Wachsmuth, and Frank Werner, Optimal regularized hypothesis testing in statistical inverse problems, §1.1

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the Hilbert adjoint and Riesz representation interfaces. The range characterization itself uses no further choice.

items.title: Gaussian posterior law in an isonormal inverse experiment
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ and $H$ be separable real Hilbert spaces with supplied finite or countable complete orthonormal bases $(v_j)$ and $(e_n)$. Let $K:X\to H$ be bounded and linear, let $\epsilon>0$, and let $U$ be a Borel Gaussian random element with mean $m_0\in X$ and positive self-adjoint, injective, trace-class covariance $C_0$. Let $Z$ be a jointly Gaussian centered family indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$, independent of $U$, and observe the random field
$$Y(g)=\langle KU,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g),\qquad g\in H,$$
on $\mathbb R^H$ with its cylinder sigma-algebra $\mathcal C_H$; write $P_Y$ for the law of this field. Write $S=C_0^{1/2}$,
$$B=SK^*KS,\qquad R=(B+\epsilon^2I_X)^{-1},\qquad C_{\rm post}=\epsilon^2SRS,$$
and for $h\in X$ put
$$\Phi_h=KSRSh.$$
For $y\in\mathbb R^H$, set
$$b_j(y)=\langle m_0,v_j\rangle_X+y(\Phi_{v_j})-\langle Km_0,\Phi_{v_j}\rangle_H.$$
If $\sum_j b_j(y)^2<\infty$, define $M_y=\sum_jb_j(y)v_j$; otherwise define $M_y=m_0$. In finite dimension these sums terminate, and an empty basis is allowed for the zero space.

There is a data-indexed probability kernel $\Pi_y$ on $X$ that is a regular conditional law of $U$ given the field $Y$, and for every $y$ it is the Borel Gaussian law with mean $M_y$ and covariance $C_{\rm post}$. In particular, for every fixed $h\in X$ and every Borel set $A\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\Pi_y\{u:\langle u,h\rangle_X\in A\}=N\!\left(\langle M_y,h\rangle_X,\langle C_{\rm post}h,h\rangle_X\right)(A).$$
For each fixed $h$, for $P_Y$-almost every $y$,
$$\langle M_y,h\rangle_X=\langle m_0,h\rangle_X+y(\Phi_h)-\langle Km_0,\Phi_h\rangle_H.$$
The exceptional null set in this identity may depend on $h$; no simultaneous identity for every $h$ on one sample set is asserted. Here $N(a,\sigma^2)$ denotes the scalar normal law of mean $a$ and variance $\sigma^2$, including the zero-variance point mass.
items.strategy: Construct the posterior mean from observation coordinates, prove the Gaussian residual is independent of the full cylinder data, and verify the conditional-law identity.

references.title: Remo Kretschmann and Frank Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, §§1.1–1.3
Andrew M. Stuart, Inverse problems: A Bayesian perspective, §6.3, Theorem 6.20 and Example 6.23
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §1.2.2

items.axiom_use: Assume the Axiom of Choice. It supplies the finite-dimensional Gaussian block independence and uniqueness interfaces used to prove that the residual is independent of the full observation sigma-algebra; Countable Choice is also used through Hilbert adjoints, square roots, and supplied bases. The countable reconstruction uses least-index choices and adds no stronger choice requirement.

items.title: Gaussian MAP feature test
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X,H$ be separable real Hilbert spaces, let $K:X\to H$ be bounded, and let $\epsilon>0$. Let $U$ be a Borel Gaussian prior with mean $m_0$ and positive self-adjoint, injective, trace-class covariance $C_0$, independent of a jointly Gaussian centered family $Z$ indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$. For parameter $x\in X$, the observation field is $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$. Fix a feature vector $h\in X$. Let
$$S=C_0^{1/2},\qquad B=SK^*KS,\qquad R=(B+\epsilon^2I_X)^{-1},\qquad \Phi_h=KSRSh,$$
and define the raw threshold
$$c_h=\langle Km_0,\Phi_h\rangle_H-\langle m_0,h\rangle_X.$$
Given a white-noise observation field $y\in\mathbb R^H$, the **Gaussian MAP feature test** returns $1$ exactly when $y(\Phi_h)>c_h$ and returns $0$ otherwise. This strict raw comparison defines the procedure for every field input $y$.

For the posterior kernel $\Pi_y$ with mean $M_y$ supplied by the Gaussian posterior-law theorem, the scalar feature marginal has mode $\langle M_y,h\rangle_X$ for every $y$, with the support point serving as the mode for a zero-variance marginal. For each fixed $h$, under that theorem's prior-predictive observation law $P_Y$, the raw rule agrees for $P_Y$-almost every $y$ with the test that returns $1$ exactly when this posterior marginal mode is positive. The exceptional null set may depend on $h$; no simultaneous equivalence for all features on one sample set is asserted.

If $h=0$, then $\Phi_h=0$ and $c_h=0$. Under every sampling law, $Y_x(0)=0$ almost surely, so the raw test returns $0$ almost surely for observations; the same holds under $P_Y$.
items.strategy: Evaluate the strict raw probe/threshold comparison for every field input; use the posterior-mode interpretation P_Y-almost surely for each fixed feature.

references.title: Remo Kretschmann and Frank Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, §1.2 and Theorems 2.3–2.5
Andrew M. Stuart, Inverse problems: A Bayesian perspective, §6.3

items.axiom_use: The procedure itself uses only the Gaussian posterior formula and a specified resolvent; the MAP interpretation inherits the Axiom of Choice required by the posterior RCD theorem.

items.title: Level, power, and weighted regularization of Gaussian MAP feature tests
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X,H$ be separable real Hilbert spaces, $K:X\to H$ bounded and linear, $\epsilon>0$, and let $U$ be a Borel Gaussian prior with mean $m_0$ and positive self-adjoint, injective, trace-class covariance $C_0$, independent of a jointly Gaussian centered family $Z$ indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$. Fix $h\in X$, define $S=C_0^{1/2}$, $B=SK^*KS$, $R=(B+\epsilon^2I)^{-1}$, $\Phi_h=KSRSh$, and $c_h=\langle Km_0,\Phi_h\rangle_H-\langle m_0,h\rangle_X$. Let $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$ and let the raw MAP test reject exactly when $Y_x(\Phi_h)>c_h$. Define $G(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-s^2/2}\,ds$, the standard normal cumulative distribution function. For every $x\in X$ its rejection probability is
$$\mathbb P_x\{Y_x(\Phi_h)>c_h\}=\begin{cases}G\!\left(\dfrac{\langle x,K^*\Phi_h\rangle_X-c_h}{\epsilon\|\Phi_h\|_H}\right),&\Phi_h\ne0,\\[6pt]\mathbf1\{0>c_h\},&\Phi_h=0.\end{cases}$$

For a further real Hilbert space $V$ continuously and injectively embedded in $X$ by $i:V\to X$, define the residual functional $r_\Phi\in V^*$, where $V^*$ is the continuous dual of $V$, by
$$r_\Phi(v)=\langle Ki(v),\Phi\rangle_H-\langle i(v),h\rangle_X,\qquad \|r_\Phi\|_{V^*}=\sup_{\|v\|_V\le1}|r_\Phi(v)|.$$
For $0<\alpha<1$ let $z_{1-\alpha}$ satisfy $G(z_{1-\alpha})=1-\alpha$. If $\Phi\ne0$, the calibrated probe test rejects exactly when
$$Y_x(\Phi)>\epsilon\|\Phi\|_H z_{1-\alpha}+\|r_\Phi\|_{V^*}.$$
Its rejection probability at every $x\in X$ is the same displayed Gaussian-tail formula with $\Phi$ in place of $\Phi_h$ and calibrated threshold in place of $c_h$. If $x=i(v)$ satisfies $\|v\|_V\le1$ and $\langle x,h\rangle_X\le0$, this test has rejection probability at most $\alpha$. For $\Phi=0$ it never rejects and has level zero.

As an additional weighted-regularization identity, assume Countable Choice and suppose that $C_0K^*K=K^*KC_0$. Let $J$ be the real partial isometry in the polar decomposition $K=J(K^*K)^{1/2}$. Let $\mathcal D=\{C_0^{1/2}x:x\in X\}$, and define $C_0^{-1/2}$ as the inverse of $C_0^{1/2}$ on $\mathcal D$. On $\Psi\in H$, set
$$J_h(\Psi)=\|K^*\Psi-h\|_X^2+\epsilon^2\|C_0^{-1/2}J^*\Psi\|_X^2$$
when $J^*\Psi\in\mathcal D$, and set $J_h(\Psi)=+\infty$ otherwise. Then $\Phi_h$ is a minimizer of $J_h$, and
$$K^*\Phi_h=B(B+\epsilon^2I_X)^{-1}h.$$
items.strategy: Derive raw and calibrated power from scalar normal tails, then minimize the weighted objective in a common eigenbasis.

references.title: Remo Kretschmann and Frank Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, Theorems 2.4–2.5
Remo Kretschmann, Tanja Wachsmuth, and Frank Werner, Optimal regularized hypothesis testing in statistical inverse problems, §1.2 and Theorem 2.3

items.axiom_use: The raw and calibrated Gaussian-tail arguments add no choice. The weighted-minimizer clause constructs the real polar partial isometry from the common eigenbasis and uses Countable Choice through the compact spectral and square-root suppliers. The posterior input inherits the Axiom of Choice from its separate RCD proof.

items.title: A non-eigenfeature can give an unrestricted Gaussian MAP test level one
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X,H$ be separable real Hilbert spaces, $K:X\to H$ bounded and linear, $\epsilon>0$, and let $U$ be a Borel Gaussian prior with mean $m_0$ and positive self-adjoint, injective, trace-class covariance $C_0$, independent of a jointly Gaussian centered family $Z$ indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$. Put $S=C_0^{1/2}$, $B=SK^*KS$, $R=(B+\epsilon^2I_X)^{-1}$. For a feature vector $h\in X$, define $\Phi_h=KSRSh$, $c_h=\langle Km_0,\Phi_h\rangle_H-\langle m_0,h\rangle_X$, and the raw test $\delta_h=\mathbf1\{Y_x(\Phi_h)>c_h\}$, where $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$. Suppose $C_0K^*K=K^*KC_0$, $h\ne0$, and $Bh$ is not a scalar multiple of $h$. Then the unrestricted null set $H_0=\{x\in X:\langle x,h\rangle_X\le0\}$ satisfies
$$\sup_{x\in H_0}\mathbb P_x\{\delta_h=1\}=1.$$
The supremum need not be attained at any finite parameter value.
items.strategy: Find a null direction orthogonal to the feature along which the raw MAP mean grows without bound.

references.title: Remo Kretschmann and Frank Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, Theorem 2.6 and its proof

items.axiom_use: The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the Gaussian posterior construction; Countable Choice is used by the shifted-operator and Hilbert-space interfaces. The null-direction scaling argument uses no further choice.

title: Linear feature identifiability and Gaussian MAP tests — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: An adjoint-range feature has an exact one-probe estimator
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $X=H=\mathbb R^2$ with the Euclidean inner product, let $K(x_1,x_2)=(x_1,x_2/2)$, fix $\epsilon>0$, and let $Z$ be a jointly Gaussian centered family on $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$. Define $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$ and consider the feature $\phi(x_1,x_2)=x_1$. The map $K$ is compact, $K^*(1,0)=(1,0)$, and the observation $Y_x(1,0)$ is an unbiased exact estimator of $\phi(x)$ with variance $\epsilon^2$. Thus the feature vector lies in the adjoint range and is exactly estimable by one probe.
items.strategy: Evaluate a finite-dimensional adjoint probe and its exact variance.

references.title: Kretschmann and Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, §1.1
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §1.2.2

items.title: A compact diagonal map has a closure-only feature
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On the real Hilbert space $X=H=\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ with standard basis $(e_j)_{j\ge1}$, define $Kx=(x_j/j)_{j\ge1}$ and the feature vector $h=(1/j)_{j\ge1}$. Fix $\epsilon>0$, let $Z$ be a jointly Gaussian centered family indexed by $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$, and define $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$. Fix $\epsilon>0$, let $Z$ be a jointly Gaussian centered family on $H$, linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$, and define $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+\epsilon Z(g)$. The map $K$ is compact and self-adjoint. Its adjoint range contains every finitely supported sequence, so $\overline{R(K^*)}=\ell^2$. The vector $h$ belongs to $\ell^2$ but not to $R(K^*)$, since any preimage would have all coordinates equal to $1$. Thus this feature lies in the closure of the adjoint range but is not exactly estimable by one probe.
items.strategy: Approximate the diagonal map by finite-rank truncations and compare the dense adjoint range with the chosen feature.

references.title: Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §1.2.2
Kretschmann and Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, §1.1

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used through the norm-limit compactness theorem. The diagonal map, density of finite sequences, and failure of exact range membership are established directly.

items.title: A non-eigenfeature gives Gaussian MAP rejection probabilities tending to one
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X=H=\mathbb R^2$, $K=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)$, $C_0=I$, $m_0=0$, and $\epsilon=1$. Let $U$ be a Borel Gaussian prior with mean $0$ and covariance $I$, independent of a jointly Gaussian centered family $Z$ on $H$ that is linear into $L^2$ with covariance $\mathbb E[Z(g)Z(k)]=\langle g,k\rangle_H$, and set $Y_x(g)=\langle Kx,g\rangle_H+Z(g)$. For $h=(1,1)$, the MAP feature operator is $B=K^*K=\operatorname{diag}(1,4)$, so $h$ is not an eigenvector. The test probe is $\Phi_h=(1/2,2/5)$ and the threshold is zero. For every $t>0$, the parameter $x_t=t(-1,1)$ is null for the feature $\langle x,h\rangle$, and the MAP test rejection probability is $G(3t/\sqrt{41})$, which tends to one as $t\to\infty$. Thus this unrestricted null class has supremum rejection probability one, although no finite $t$ attains it.
items.strategy: Calculate the finite-dimensional MAP probe and evaluate its rejection tail along a null ray.

references.title: Kretschmann and Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems, Theorem 2.6
